document.title: Turkmenistan and Pakistan Predict War, Even While "Working for Peace," In Afghanistan, and Continue to Support Taliban (Islamabad 01462)
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), "No-Go" Tribal Areas Became Basis for Afghan Insurgency Documents Show
document.note: [Confidential] A protected source tells U.S. officials that the Taliban are "here to stay" and that Pakistan will always support them despite U.S. objections. Pakistan cannot change this for fear of rebellion across the NWFP, FATA and the Pashtun border area. Musharraf-Mullah Rabbani talks in January 2000 were cordial and raised terrorism. The source claims the Taliban are growing, moderating and have countrywide support. The embassy commentary is excised.

key_claims: A Turkmen interlocutor said Pakistan 'will always support the Taliban' and policy cannot change.
Both countries expect continued Taliban–Northern Alliance fighting and eventual Taliban victory.
The Taliban were said to be 'looking for a way out' of the bin Ladin problem and to reject a loya jirga.
Musharraf's raising of terrorism with Rabbani was characterized as cordial, with no concessions.
